quarterly_data.signal: CEO sized AI inside the whole company for the first time at this level of detail: the AI business has been 'maybe about 40% of our growth this year', with the rest coming from energy infrastructure, aerospace and defense and above-market automotive content.
quarterly_data.figure: AI business about 40% of our growth this year; TE's going to grow about $2.5 billion this year

quarterly_data.signal: DDN (the AI/cloud business) sized and its power/data mix trajectory given: DDN is 'about $3 billion of our $20 billion this year' and power connections have gone from roughly a quarter of DDN three years ago to about a third today, a share management expects to keep rising as rack power architectures change. Customers looking at 800-volt sidecar power racks that support the GPU racks are the specific driver — those architectures 'can create a 50% increase in our content on a rack'. DDN is delivering around $1 billion of growth this year.
quarterly_data.figure: DDN about $3 billion of our $20 billion this year; power connectivity 25% of our DDN business three years ago, up to 30%/about a third now; 800V sidecar racks a 50% increase in our content on a rack; DDN growth around $1 billion this year

quarterly_data.signal: Energy (grid/utility connectivity that feeds data-center power) raised to mid-teens growth and management says that rate is repeatable going forward: the end market itself went from a 1%-2% market five years ago to 6%-7% today, TE is 70% U.S.-focused there (strongest in medium voltage and undergrounding), and is adding capacity in New Jersey and Ohio after the Richards and Harger acquisitions. Utility-scale solar is the renewables exposure and is running slower on regulation; Europe is now stepping up investment (including LNG facilities).
quarterly_data.figure: energy mid-teens growth this year in a market growing 6%-7% today versus a 1%-2% market five years ago; 70% of our business is U.S.-focused
